[context] Psalms 118:48 And I lifted up my hands to thy commandments which I loved; and I meditated in thine ordinances.
Psalms 118:49 Remember thy words to thy servant, wherein thou hast made me hope.
Psalms 118:50 This has comforted me in mine affliction: for thine oracle has quickened me.
Psalms 118:51 The proud have transgressed exceedingly; but I swerved not from thy law.
Psalms 118:52 I remembered thy judgments of old, O Lord; and was comforted.
Psalms 118:53 Despair took hold upon me, because of the sinners who forsake thy law.
Psalms 118:54 Thine ordinances were my songs in the place of my sojourning.
Psalms 118:55 I remembered thy name, O Lord, in the night, and kept thy law.
Psalms 118:56 This I had, because I diligently sought thine ordinances.
Psalms 118:57 Thou art my portion, O Lord: I said that I would keep thy law.
Psalms 118:58 I besought thy favour with my whole heart: have mercy upon me according to thy word.
Psalms 118:59 I thought on thy ways, and turned my feet to thy testimonies.
Psalms 118:60 I prepared myself, (and was not terrified,) to keep thy commandments.
Psalms 118:61 The snares of sinners entangled me: but I forgot not thy law.
Psalms 118:62 At midnight I arose, to give thanks to thee for the judgments of thy righteousness.
Psalms 118:63 I am a companion of all them that fear thee, and of them that keep thy commandments.
Psalms 118:64 O Lord, the earth is full of thy mercy: teach me thine ordinances.
Psalms 118:65 Thou hast wrought kindly with thy servant, o Lord, according to thy word.
Psalms 118:66 Teach me kindness, and instruction, and knowledge: for I have believed thy commandments.
Psalms 118:67 Before I was afflicted, I transgressed; therefore have I kept thy word.
Psalms 118:68 Good art thou, O Lord; therefore in thy goodness teach me thine ordinances.
Psalms 118:69 The injustice of the proud has been multiplied against me: but I will search out thy commandments with all my heart.
Psalms 118:70 Their heart has been curdled like milk; but I have meditated on thy law.
Psalms 118:71 It is good for me that thou hast afflicted me; that I might learn thine ordinances.
[context] Psalms 118:72 The law of thy mouth is better to me than thousands of gold and silver.

translations.T1:
# Psalm cxviii. 49—60. | 129 | Psalm cxviii. 61—71.

STATUTES.

Z. ZAI

49. Remember your word to your
    servant, in which you made me hope.
50. This is my comfort
    in my affliction;
    for your word has quickened me.
51. The proud have acted lawlessly,
    I did not turn away from your law.
52. I remembered your judgments from
    eternity, O Lord, and I was comforted.
53. Grief has taken hold of me
    because of the sinners who have
    forsaken your law.
54. Your statutes were
    my psalms in the place of
    my sojourn.
55. I remembered your name in the
    night, and I kept your law.
56. This has happened to me because I sought
    after your statutes.

H. HETH

57. You are my portion, O Lord; I have said
    that I would keep your words.
58. I entreated your favor with my whole
    heart.
59. I have turned my feet to your
    testimonies, according to your word;
    I considered your testimonies.
60. I was prepared for the disturbance,
    to keep your commandments.

<column-break/>

61. The ropes of the sinners have surrounded me;
    I have not forgotten your law.
62. I will rise at midnight
    to confess to you
    the words of your righteousness.
63. I am a companion of all who fear
    you,
    and who keep your commandments.
64. The earth is full of your mercy, O Lord;
    teach me your statutes.

T. TETH

65. O Lord, you have dealt with goodness
    with your servant.
66. O Lord, according to your word, teach
    me goodness,
    and instruction, and knowledge;
    for I have believed in your commandments.
67. I sinned before I was
    humbled; therefore I have kept your words.
68. You are good; teach me
    your statutes in your
    goodness.
69. The craftiness of the proud
    has multiplied against me;
    but I will seek after your
    ways with my whole heart.
70. Their heart is thickened like
    curds;
    but I have meditated on your
    law.
71. It is good for me that you have humbled me;
    that I might learn your statutes.

<summary>This page continues Psalm 118, emphasizing the psalmist's steadfastness in the law despite affliction and the deceit of the proud.</summary>
<keywords>Psalm 118, law, statutes, humility, sinners, meditation</keywords>

that the Lord established with you. And I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights; I did not eat bread or drink water.
<margin>10</margin> And the Lord gave me the two stone tablets written with the finger of God; and on them were written all the words that the Lord spoke to you on the mountain, on the day you were gathered together.
<margin>11</margin> And it happened after forty days and forty nights, the Lord gave me the two stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant.
<margin>12</margin> And the Lord said to me, "Arise and go down quickly from here, for your people whom you brought out of the land of Egypt have acted wickedly <note>original: "aϥaнoмєi", Greek: ἠνόμησεν</note>. They have turned aside <note>original: "aυpapaвa", Greek: παρέβησαν</note> quickly from the way that I commanded them; they have made for themselves a molten image."
<margin>13</margin> And the Lord said to me, "I have spoken to you once and twice, saying: 'I have seen this people, and behold, they are a stiff-necked <note>original: "naϣt мakϩ", translated as stubborn/stiff-necked</note> people.'
<margin>14</margin> Let me alone, so that I may destroy them and blot out their name from under heaven; and I will make you into a great and strong nation, and more numerous than these."

<summary>Moses recounts the Lord's instructions to descend the mountain after the people made a golden calf, and God's threat to destroy them and raise a new nation through Moses.</summary>

Psalms 54:5 My heart was troubled within me; and the fear of death fell upon me.
Psalms 54:6 Fear and trembling came upon me, and darkness covered me.
Psalms 54:7 And I said, O that I had wings as those of a dove! then would I flee away, and be at rest.
Psalms 54:8 Lo! I have fled afar off, and lodged in the wilderness. Pause.
Psalms 54:9 I waited for him that should deliver me from distress of spirit and tempest.
Psalms 54:10 Destroy, O Lord, and divide their tongues: for I have seen iniquity and gain saying in the city.
Psalms 54:11 Day and night he shall go round about it upon its walls: iniquity and sorrow and unrighteousness are in the midst of it;
Psalms 54:12 and usury and craft have not failed from its streets.
Psalms 54:13 For if an enemy had reproached me, I would have endured it; and if one who hated me had spoken vauntingly against me, I would have hid myself from him.
Psalms 54:14 But thou, O man like minded, my guide, and my acquaintance,
Psalms 54:15 who in companionship with me sweetened our food: we walked in the house of God in concord.
Psalms 54:16 Let death come upon them, and let them go down alive into Hades, for iniquity is in their dwellings, in the midst of them.
Psalms 54:17 I cried to God, and the Lord hearkened to me.
Psalms 54:18 Evening, and morning, and at noon I will declare and make known my wants: and he shall hear my voice.
Psalms 54:19 He shall deliver my soul in peace from them that draw nigh to me: for they were with me in many cases.
Psalms 54:20 God shall hear, and bring them low, even he that has existed from eternity. Pause. For they suffer no reverse, and therefore they have not feared God.
Psalms 54:21 He has reached forth his hand for retribution; they have profaned his covenant.
[context] Psalms 54:22 They were scattered at the anger of his countenance, and his heart drew nigh them. His words were smoother than oil, yet are they darts.

translations.T1:
# Psalm 54. 4—13. 58 Psalm 54. 14—21.

4. My heart is troubled within me, and the fear of death has fallen upon me. 5. Fear and trembling have come upon me, and darkness has covered me. 6. And I said, Who will give me wings like a dove? I will fly away and be at rest. <note>Selah</note> 7. Lo, I have wandered far, I have fled, and I have lodged in the wilderness. 8. I waited for him who would save me from faintness of spirit and from the storm. 9. Confuse, O Lord, and divide their tongues, for I have seen iniquity and gainsaying in the city. 10. By day and by night they shall circle around it upon its walls; iniquity and trouble are in its midst. 11. And unrighteousness is in its midst, and usury and deceit have not departed from its streets. 12. For if an enemy had reproached me, I would have borne it; and if he who hates me had spoken great words against me, I would have hidden myself from him. 13. But you, O man, who are of one mind with me, my guide and my acquaintance,

<column-break/>

14. who together with me would eat of the sweet food; we would walk in the house of God with one accord. 15. Let death come upon them; let them go down alive into Hades, for wickedness is in their dwelling places, in their midst. 16. But I have cried out to God, and the Lord has listened to me. 17. I will speak at the time of evening, and morning, and at noonday; I will cry out, and he shall listen to my voice. 18. He shall ransom my soul in peace from those who are against me, for there were many with me. 19. God shall hear, and humble them, he who is before the ages. <note>Selah</note> There is no changing for them, and they did not fear God. 20. He has stretched out his hand in retribution; he has defiled his covenant. 21. They were divided by the anger of his face, and his heart has drawn near; his words are softer than oil.

translations.T1:
# JONAH I. 12—II. 3

...Jonah said to them, "Take me and cast me into the sea, and the sea will be calm for you, because I know for my sake this great storm is upon you." 
13 But the men were struggling to bring the boat back to land, but they could not, because the sea was raging very much against them. 
14 And they cried out to the Lord, saying, "Do not be angry with us, O Lord, do not let us die because of the soul of this man, and do not bring upon us innocent blood, because you, O Lord, have done as you wished." 
15 And they took Jonah and cast him into the sea, and the sea became calm. 
16 And the men feared the Lord with a great fear, and they sacrificed a sacrifice to the Lord. 

<margin>Fol. 55 a </margin>
Chap. II. 1
17 And the Lord ordered a great sea creature <term>ketos</term> to swallow Jonah. And Jonah was inside the <insert>creature</insert> for three days and three nights. 
2 And Jonah prayed to the Lord his God while he was inside the sea creature, 
3 saying, "I cried out of my distress to the Lord my God, and he heard..."

<note>¹ Greek: παραβιάζοντο (they were forcing/struggling).</note>
<note>² 'Be not wroth with us, O Lord'; Greek: μηδαμῶς κύριε.</note>
